Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Apex Asset Management Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Asset Management's Q3 results. Joining me on today's call are Mark Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Jane Ellis, Chief Financial Officer; Sarah Thompson, Chief Investment Officer; Tom Hargrove, Head of Distribution; and Lisa Chen, Head of Operations.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Mark Reynolds.

Mark Reynolds: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q3. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by exceptional fund performance across our equity, fixed income, and alternatives strategies that outpaced peers and benchmarks. Our AUM grew to $1.78 trillion.

Jane Ellis: Thank you, Mark. From a financial perspective, Apex Asset Management delivered strong results in Q3. Our revenue was $1.38 billion, representing a 14% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by robust AUM expansion and favorable fee dynamics. Let me provide some details on our assets under management first, as it's the foundation of our results.

As of September 30th, our total AUM stood at $1.78 trillion, reflecting a solid 12% year-over-year increase and 4% quarter-over-quarter growth. This performance exceeded our peer group, such as BlackRock's 9% YoY growth or Vanguard's 7%, thanks to $28 billion in strong net inflows during the quarter, $42 billion in market appreciation from a supportive equity rally, and $5 billion in foreign exchange tailwinds, mainly from a softer USD versus the EUR and certain APAC currencies.

Geographically, we're well-diversified. North America accounts for 52% of total AUM at $926 billion, up 15% YoY, powered by $18 billion in net new money, mostly into passive equity ETFs and alternatives. Institutional flows led with $12 billion from defined contribution plans and sovereign wealth funds into products like our S&P 500 ESG ETF, now at $45 billion AUM with 2.5% market share in sustainable large caps. Retail added $6 billion via RIA partnerships, supported by the Nasdaq rally where our active growth strategies delivered 18% annualized returns, beating benchmarks by 450 basis points. Fixed income saw some short-duration outflows of $2 billion, balanced by shifts to private credit.

Europe represents 24% at $427 billion, expanding 10% YoY with $6 billion in net new money amid economic challenges. The UK and Nordics contributed 60%, driven by UCITS-compliant sustainable multi-asset funds like our Eurozone Green Transition Fund at €25 billion AUM, aligning with EU SFDR and net-zero mandates, securing €4 billion from pension funds under TCFD. Germany and France were softer due to fiscal pressures, but platform integrations with Allfunds and FundRock stabilized flows. FX added €2 billion. We're expanding private markets with a €5 billion pan-European real assets vehicle partnering with firms like Ardian to access €300 billion in unallocated EU pension capital.

Asia-Pacific, at 16% or $285 billion, grew fastest at 22% YoY on $7 billion net inflows and currency gains in JPY and AUD. China and India drove 55%, with Hong Kong platforms directing $4 billion into Asia ex-Japan equities returning 22% on the CSI 300 rebound. Mumbai added $3 billion in alternatives like our India Infrastructure Debt Fund amid digital economy growth. Japan holds steady at ¥40 trillion with GPIF favoring active sleeves. Our Aladdin-powered robo-advisory, compliant with MAS guidelines, onboarded 150,000 HNW clients, lifting recurring fees 15%.

Rest of World is 8% at $142 billion, up 8%, led by LatAm sovereigns at $40 billion and MENA SWFs at $50 billion. Brazil pensions brought $2 billion to EM debt, and UAE ties with ADIA grow Sharia-compliant ESG.

Moving to expenses, we reported $980 million, resulting in net income of $355 million. Our expense ratio improved to 68% due to scale efficiencies and targeted investments. Diving deeper, operating expenses totaled $980 million in Q3, up 5% YoY from $935 million, or 68 basis points of average AUM—stable sequentially but with modest expansion reflecting inflation and growth initiatives. This drove operating margins to 37%, highlighting leverage in our fee model across $320 billion in passive ETFs and $285 billion in alternatives like direct lending and infrastructure.

Compensation and benefits were $539 million, 55% of OpEx, up 8% YoY from performance incentives on our revenue outperformance, 4.5% merit increases for our 2,800 global staff, and retention bonuses for PMs in quant and ESG. Headcount rose 1% QoQ in APAC multi-asset amid $5 billion SWF inflows. U.S. costs up 10% from competition, EMEA flat post-Brexit. We expect mid-single-digit growth in H2, offset by AI tools cutting analyst hours 20%.

Distribution, marketing, and servicing hit $40 million, 15% of OpEx, up 2% YoY, covering subadvisory on $120 billion intermediary channels like 401(k)s and RIAs, plus ETF marketing amid 25 bps fee pressure to match Vanguard. $8 million went to Schwab/Fidelity TAMP partnerships driving $3 billion RIA flows. We're allocating 30% to digital like LinkedIn and podcasts for 3x ROI, with APAC up 5% on roadshows.

G&A was $53 million, 20% of OpEx, up 4% YoY. Occupancy $12 million flat with hybrid 70% utilization across NYC, London, Mumbai. Professional fees up 7% to $18 million for SEC prep and SFDR. Travel $9 million up 15% for LP meetings on $40 billion private credit fundraising, offset by $2 million vendor savings.

Technology and data $23 million, 8% up 15% YoY, with $7 million capex for AWS migration slashing OMS latency 40% and enabling real-time ESG scoring on $100 billion mandates. Data feeds $10 million including alt data for EM alpha. Our platform handles 95% of $300 billion institutional, saving 15% OpEx. EMEA up 20% for MiFID II, U.S. for Reg BI.

Other $5 million flat, mainly intangibles amortization.

Overall, OpEx trailed revenue growth, with $50 million tech roadmap including AI for inflows and zero-based G&A targeting 3-5 bps compression. U.S. intensity 75 bps, EMEA 55 bps, APAC 45 bps. Full-year OpEx $1.15-1.18 billion for 38%+ margins.

Turning to forward guidance for Q4 and full-year 2024, incorporating base assumptions on markets, flows, elevated rates, moderating inflation, AI equity upside from NVIDIA/Microsoft, EM/Europe geopolitics, and U.S. retirement inflows.

Q4 revenues $1.45-$1.50 billion, 8-11% sequential, 12-15% YoY; full-year $5.75-$5.85 billion, up 14%. Management fees ~85% at $1.25-$1.28 billion on ending AUM $1.85-$1.90 trillion, average $1.82 trillion at 72 bps, shifting to active/alts. Equity up 4-6% QoQ on markets/$15-18B inflows, AI ETF $2.5B YTD. FI 28% AUM, $12-15B inflows, fees +18% YoY.

Performance fees $120-$150M up from $95M on hedge FoFs/private credit; Global Equity Partners +22% YTD vs MSCI +450 bps.

Distribution/other $80-$90M on $8-10B retail via Schwab/Fidelity.

Flows: Q4 $45-55B net long-term, full-year ~$180B; institutional 55%, retail +10-12% YoY on Apex Wealth 2.5M users/15% millennial RIA share. U.S. 65% ($30-35B), Europe 20% despite MiFID trailer compression 5-7 bps, APAC/EM 15% $7B on China A/India small-cap.

Product innovation: Q4 $500M tokenized PE on Fireblocks blockchain, ESG muni ladder ETF for $1B YE. Alts 22% AUM at 120 bps.

Expenses: full-year $3.95-$4.05B, +5-7% YoY, ratio 68.5-69.5% down 50 bps; Q4 $1.05-$1.08B.

Comp $575-$590M Q4 (55%), variable 45% tied to flows/perf; full comp ~38% revenues, +250 advisors, no back-office.

G&A/occupancy $220-$230M flat post-45 office consolidation.

Marketing/dist/tech $255-$260M +12% YoY, $150M tech incl AI alpha (20% backtest outperf), GenAI chatbots -15% call costs, OMS for +30% ETF trades.

Margins 30.5-31.5%, EPS $4.85-$4.95; pursuing private markets M&A with $2-3B powder like BlackRock GIP. APAC 85% margins, Europe 72% SFDR. Alts gross 65% by 2026, perf/alts 25% revenues.

This supports 12-15% organic revenue CAGR to 2027 via alts/digital/EM.

Now, on capital allocation, with record fee revenues up 12% YoY to support, we prioritize ROIC at 22% after-tax. Past 12 months $6.2B deployed, 95% FCF, 15% TSR beating KBW by 400 bps.

Shareholder distributions 65%: Q3 $850M buybacks at $142 avg retiring 2.1% float, 18% ROIC; YTD $2.9B, dividend $0.85/share +6%, 2.1% yield. Data-driven vs DCF 7-9% CAGR, 1.2x net debt/EBITDA, $4.1B liquidity; accelerate below 14x P/E.

Reinvestments 25%: $450M tech/dist +20% YoY. Digital $180M GAP Horizon robo for +15% QoQ RIA flows, $12B ETF YTD, 22% ETF franchise. Alts $150M evergreen credit/infra; alts $285B +22%, 85 bps; $5B data center REIT w/DigitalBridge 12-15% IRRs AI. Talent $120M quant/AI w/Two Sigma, $180B systematic.

APAC 18% AUM +$18B HK/SG China/yen; Europe €9B SFDR; U.S. retail 42% flows.

M&A 10% flexible: 7 deals $8.5B since '22 accretive; Q3 $1.2B Summit Edge $55B credit 95 bps/25% margins like PIMCO; private credit $120B for $1.7T powder. 12-15x multiples LDI/UK opps; $3.2B powder 2-3 bolt-ons '25.

Flexes w/inflation real assets, Fed cuts pension flows. Risks EM 10%, beta compression; 45% active +20 bps 3-yr. FY25 $7.5-8B deploy 20%+ ROIC, compounding BVPS 13%/5 yrs >10% hurdle.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Jane. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities and alternatives. Overall, our core equity strategies returned 11.8% in Q3, surpassing the MSCI World by 320 bps and median Morningstar peers by 450 bps. Fixed income yielded 4.2%, ahead of Bloomberg U.S. Aggregate by 110 bps and 78% Lipper peers. Alternatives netted 7.5%, topping Cambridge by 180 bps, fueling 14% QoQ AUM to $285 billion and $12.4 billion inflows—strongest since Q4 2021.

In equities, Large-Cap Growth at $45 billion AUM returned 15.2% vs Russell 1000 Growth 12.1% and VUG by 410 bps, from AI infra like Nvidia +28%, cloud. Vs BlackRock IWF 11.9%. Large-Cap Value $32 billion 9.8% vs 8.2%, Fidelity median +280 bps; JPM/Exxon financials/energy, quant dividend growers +90 bps.

SMID 6.5% vs Russell 2000 4.1%/Midcap 3.9%, top 92% peers; U.S. reshoring, Europe Pan-Euro 5.2% vs STOXX 3.8% Siemens; APAC ex-Jpn 7.1% vs MSCI +250 bps Tencent stimulus vs Fidelity. EM Alpha 10.4% vs MSCI 8.2% +220 bps India/Mexico, FX hedges.

Fixed income Core Bond 4.1% vs Agg 3.0%/PIMCO +90 bps, duration to 6.2 yrs 4.75% IG, HY 5.8% vs ICE +140 bps CCC energy vs BND 3.2%. Muni 3.9% vs S&P +80 bps 85% peers.

Multi-asset 7.2% vs 60/40 5.9% +130 bps; ESG 22% AUM, Sustainable Global 12.1% vs MSCI ESG 10.8%.

Alts $52 billion +18% YoY; private credit 8.2% vs Cliffwater +150 bps 11% IRRs software; infra 6.9% CPI+400 bps data centers; top quartile 14.2% Preqin vs Blackstone.

Drivers: stock selection 55% equity alpha, QARP screen 25%+ names. Apex AI Optimizer 2.0 NLP/reinforcement +0.15 Sharpe; ESG engine 95% SFDR $4.2B EU. U.S. 68%, EMEA +22% MiFID ETFs, APAC China reopen. Deglobalization industrials/onshoring, 10% EM cash.

IR 0.85 vs peer 0.42, drawdown -2.1% vs -3.8%, vol 11-13%. Outlook constructive S&P 5800 selective, FI 4.5-5% carry, munis post-tax; AI harvest defensives healthcare/utilities. Active prowess 2-4% net alpha at 1.2% fees vs passive commoditization.

We're navigating the current market by emphasizing quality stock selection and AI-enhanced risk management. We launched our AI Infrastructure ETF this quarter, and early reception has been positive, with $2.5 billion in YTD flows and strong institutional adoption.

Tom Hargrove: Thank you, Sarah. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our equity and ETF funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in Asia-Pacific are paying off, as evidenced by $7 billion in regional net new money, accelerated growth in China A-shares and India small-cap products leveraging post-COVID rebound, and partnerships onboarding 150,000 HNW clients via localized robo-advisory tools.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Tom. Operationally, we've made significant progress in improving our technology infrastructure, including $150 million in FY tech spend on AI-driven alpha generation piloted for 20% outperformance, GenAI chatbots reducing call center costs by 15%, AWS cloud migration cutting OMS latency 40%, and scaling for 30% more ETF trades. This has resulted in increased efficiency, 15% OpEx savings on institutional mandates, and reduced operational risk. We're also focused on regulatory compliance upgrades like MiFID II reporting and SEC Reg BI tools.

Mark Reynolds: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes sustained AUM expansion through diversified channels and product innovation.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from Sarah Thompson with Morningstar.

Sarah Thompson: Thanks, and good morning, team. I wanted to dive into your AUM outlook. With markets volatile amid Fed rate cut expectations and geopolitical tensions, can you walk us through management's expectations for AUM growth over the next 12-18 months? Specifically, how do you see organic versus inorganic contributions, and any color on product mix or regional flows?

Mark Reynolds: Great question, Sarah. Jane will start with the high-level outlook, then I'll add strategic color. 

Jane Ellis: Thanks, Mark. We ended Q3 at $1.78 trillion AUM, up 12% QoQ and 22% YoY from 7% market appreciation on S&P 18% YTD and Magnificent Seven overweight, plus $42 billion NNM at 3.1% organic quarterly.

For FY2025, we guide 10-12% growth to $1.96-$1.99 trillion end-2025: 6-8% markets/FX assuming MSCI World 7-9%, Fed 4.25-4.50%; 4-6% organic $75-90 billion NNM. Conservative on U.S. elections/China property.

Mark Reynolds: Thanks, Jane. Diversification stress-tested vs 10% drawdown or 3%+ inflation. Organic North Star: H2 FY25 $25-30 billion quarterly NNM from Q3 $18 billion. Institutional $28 billion YTD into Global Alpha Fund +250 bps alpha vs Fidelity Contrafund. Retail ETFs $250 billion incl HESG 15% sustainable share, 28 bps fees.

Innovation: Q1 2025 three active ETFs—AI/Automation 20% target NVIDIA/ASML/private; short-duration credit; alts-linked UCITS to $120 billion privates. Horizon AI robo 97% retention, NLP personalization vs Vanguard.

Regions: U.S. 55% 8-10% DC/RIA $15 billion Envestnet. EMEA 30% 15% MiFID €20 billion Nordic SFDR Amundi rivals. APAC 15% 20-25% DBS JV $10 billion Nikkei/India 8% GDP; China $2 billion H-shares.

Inorganic 2-3% $50 billion powder tuck-ins like Vertex One +50 bps alts fees to 45 bps blended. NPS 72, $150 million cloud risk platform.

Resilient to 5% markets; alpha/beta blend superior growth.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you.

Operator: Our next question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of our Global Equity Partners composite?

Sarah Thompson: Good morning, John. Our flagship Global Equity Partners composite is up 22% YTD, outpacing the MSCI World by 450 basis points, with asset-weighted equity strategies at 11.8% Q3 return versus 320 bps over the index and 450 bps over peers. Large-cap growth led at 15.2% versus Russell 1000 Growth, driven by AI positions, while EM Alpha added 220 bps on India and Mexico. Risk-adjusted metrics like 0.85 information ratio confirm our edge.

John Smith: And how is the new AI Infrastructure ETF performing relative to expectations?

Tom Hargrove: Thanks for the follow-up. The AI Infrastructure ETF has exceeded expectations with $2.5 billion in YTD flows, capturing significant institutional interest and contributing to equity AUM growth of 4-6% QoQ projected. Early traction mirrors our tokenized PE seed and ESG muni launches, aligning with client demand for thematic and illiquid strategies now at 22% of AUM.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan.

Emily Chen: Can you provide more color on the operational efficiencies you've gained?

Lisa Chen: Good morning, Emily. Our tech investments have delivered tangible gains: AI alpha tools show 20% backtest outperformance, GenAI chatbots cut call costs 15%, OMS scales 30% more ETF trades with 40% less latency via AWS, and platform automation saves 15% on $300 billion mandates. Hybrid occupancy at 70% utilization and vendor consolidation clawed back millions, targeting 3-5 bps AUM compression. Regional efficiencies shine in APAC at 45 bps intensity.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Mark Reynolds for closing remarks.

Mark Reynolds: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Asset Management. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
